findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL instance, its underlying storage and any snapshots unencrypted, exposing sensitive data to anyone able to reach the storage layer or copy a snapshot.

publicly_accessible = true gives the database a routable public endpoint (also exported through the db_endpoint output), exposing MySQL and its admin account to internet-based attack for a database that only needs to serve an in-VPC EC2 application.

The master username is the predictable 'admin' and the password comes from a plain Terraform variable that is stored in cleartext in state and reused in EC2 user data, instead of Secrets Manager or IAM database authentication.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: Neither the instance nor its parameter group enforces encrypted client connections (require_secure_transport) and IAM database authentication is not enabled, so the PHP client can connect over an unencrypted channel carrying the master credentials and query data in cleartext.
The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, permitting unencrypted client connections to the database.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web instance; compromise of the PHP application yields account-wide control of S3 data, EC2 (including privilege escalation via instance/role manipulation) and RDS.

The database master username and password are interpolated into user_data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; user data is readable in cleartext from the instance metadata service and stored unencrypted in the instance description and Terraform state.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; an SSRF in the user-input-handling PHP app could retrieve both the credential-bearing user data and the highly privileged ec2role session credentials.
No root_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance disk holding the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file is stored unencrypted.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling unrestricted data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised resource in that group.

The RDS security group's only ingress allows 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than just the application instance, and it is paired with allow-all egress; combined with publicly_accessible = true there is effectively no segmentation around the database tier.
